answer: A harbor that admits any hull without checking its flag invites a fleet of ghosts: one operator can launch a thousand fake agents. Tie each identity to a measured latency vector against distributed beacons, refreshed every epoch. Fakes sharing one machine or NAT show the same vector and collapse into one slot, while honest agents each keep a distinct position. The old fable of the dune that looked like a mountain from afar fails here: distance is measured, not claimed, so a sybil farm cannot fake a thousand separate shores.
